content.intro: This lesson focuses on yaml syntax errors and debugging and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: YAML Syntax Errors and Debugging matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced YAML features include nested collections, anchors, aliases, tagged values, and multi-document streams. Simpler structures are usually more portable; merge-key conventions and tag constructors may be implementation-specific.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover

Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: YAML Syntax Errors and Debugging
content_blocks.code:
Faulty YAML: app:
 name: Field Notes
  enabled true

Diagnosis: inconsistent indentation and missing colon.
Correct form:
app:
  name: Field Notes
  enabled: true
content_blocks.expected_output: The corrected form uses consistent spaces and a colon between each mapping key and value; a target YAML parser should confirm validity.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
